Dynamic (multi-season) false-positive occupancy model

Source: R/fp_occu_dyn.R
fp_occu_dyn.Rd

Fits a false-positive occupancy model over several seasons (primary periods), in which the occupancy state of each site changes between seasons by colonization and extinction. Within each season the observation model is that of fp_occu(): the multiple-methods and observation-confirmation designs, verified detections, recorder and site effects, false-positive covariates and runs of detections. This function is experimental (see crywolf-api): its arguments, results and output names may change in a minor version.

Usage

fp_occu_dyn(
  data,
  psi1 = ~1,
  col = ~1,
  ext = ~1,
  det = ~1,
  fp = ~1,
  random_recorder = !is.null(data$recorder),
  ver = ~1,
  markov = NULL,
  random_fp = FALSE,
  random_det = FALSE,
  priors = fp_priors(),
  chains = 4,
  parallel_chains = chains,
  threads_per_chain = "auto",
  iter_warmup = 1000,
  iter_sampling = 1000,
  adapt_delta = 0.95,
  seed = NULL,
  refresh = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu_dyn'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu_dyn'
summary(object, prob = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu_dyn'
as_draws_df(x, ...)

Arguments

data

An fp_data object with a season column; see the season and season_covs arguments of fp_data().

psi1

One-sided formula for the occupancy probability in the first season. It may use site covariates and covariates of the first season.

col, ext

One-sided formulas for the colonization and extinction probabilities. They may use site covariates and season covariates (fp_data(season_covs = )). All three formulas keep their intercept, with the priors of fp_priors() for intercepts and slopes.

det, fp, random_recorder, ver, markov, random_fp, random_det, priors

As in fp_occu(); formulas may also use season covariates. markov runs of detections do not cross seasons. Site effects (random_fp, random_det) belong to sites and are shared by their seasons.

chains, parallel_chains, threads_per_chain, iter_warmup, iter_sampling, adapt_delta, seed, refresh, ...

Passed to the sampler, as in fp_occu().

x, object

An fp_occu_dyn object.

digits

Number of digits to print.

prob

Width of the equal-tailed credible interval.

Value

An object of class fp_occu_dyn, a list with fit, draws (readable names: see crywolf-output), stan_data, formulas (psi1, col, ext, det, fp, ver), markov, design, data, random_recorder, random_fp, random_det, priors, sampler, diagnostics and call. Its methods are print(), summary(), as_draws_df() and simulate(); fp_sites() gives the occupancy of each site-season and fp_ppc() checks the fit.

summary() returns an object of class summary.fp_occu, as for fp_occu(), whose table has also a season column: the season of the derived quantities psi_mean[t], psi_fs[t] and turnover[t], and empty for the other rows (see crywolf-output).

Details

The occupancy state of site \(i\) in the first season is Bernoulli with probability \(\psi_{1,i}\). In each later season \(t\), an occupied site stays occupied with probability \(1 - \epsilon_{it}\) (extinction \(\epsilon\)) and an unoccupied one becomes occupied with probability \(\gamma_{it}\) (colonization), on the logit scale linear in the covariates of col and ext. The covariates of a transition are those of the season it enters (row \(t\) of the site-season table for the transition from \(t - 1\) to \(t\)). The states are summed out by the forward algorithm, so the log-likelihood (log_lik) is per site, over all its seasons.

A site without data in a season contributes to that season only through the transitions. With seasons that are dates, fp_data() fills in the missing dates, so colonization and extinction are probabilities per step (per night, for nightly seasons). A single false positive looks like a colonization followed by an extinction: without verified or confirmed data in the seasons, the two processes are hard to separate from false positives.

The fit also gives, per season, the expected and the realized occupancy over sites (psi_mean, psi_fs) and the turnover, and, with constant transitions, the equilibrium occupancy (psi_eq); see crywolf-output. summary() lists them with their season; print() shows only the parameters.

See also

fp_data(), fp_occu(), simulate_fp_dyn(), crywolf-output; vignette("dynamic") fits it to the curiango data, with the nights of each site as seasons.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
s <- simulate_fp_dyn(nsite = 150, nseason = 4, b_col = 1, b_ext = -1, seed = 1)
m <- fp_occu_dyn(s$data, psi1 = ~ x, col = ~ rain, ext = ~ x,
                 random_recorder = FALSE)
m
head(fp_sites(m))   # one row per site-season
} # }
